record.original_question: Let Diag be the class of Turing degrees d such that every computably enumerable equivalence relation E ≠ Id_1 admits a d-computable diagonal function g with g(x) not E-equivalent to x for all x. Determine (i) the class Diag; (ii) the reverse-mathematical strength of the statement that every Σ^0_1-definable equivalence relation E ≠ Id_1 has a diagonal function; and (iii) the Weihrauch degree of the associated problem.

evidence.quote: Ceer stands for computably enumerable equivalence relation on ω. A diagonal function (or a fixed-point-free function) for a ceer E is a total function g(x) satisfying ¬g(x)Ex for all x ∈ ω.
Problem 25. The following are three versions of this problem. (i) Describe the class Diag containing those Turing degrees d such that every ceer E ̸= Id1 admits a d-computable diagonal function.

(ii) What is the reverse-mathematical strength of the statement 'Every Σ0_1-definable equivalence relation E ̸= Id1 has a diagonal function'? (iii) What is the Weihrauch degree of the corresponding problem?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
A computably enumerable equivalence relation (ceer) is an equivalence relation $E$ on $\omega = \{0,1,2,\dots\}$ whose graph $\{(x,y) : x\,E\,y\}$ is computably enumerable. Let $\mathrm{Id}_1$ denote the equivalence relation on $\omega$ with a single equivalence class (i.e., $x\,\mathrm{Id}_1\,y$ for all $x,y$). For an equivalence relation $E$ on $\omega$, a diagonal function (or fixed-point-free function) for $E$ is a total function $g:\omega\to\omega$ such that $\neg(g(x)\,E\,x)$ for every $x\in\omega$.

Given a Turing degree $\mathbf d$, say that $\mathbf d \in \mathrm{Diag}$ iff for every ceer $E\neq \mathrm{Id}_1$ there exists a $\mathbf d$-computable diagonal function for $E$.

Address the following three questions.

(i) Characterize the class $\mathrm{Diag}$ of Turing degrees.

(ii) Determine the reverse-mathematical strength (over $\mathrm{RCA}_0$) of the statement: "Every $\Sigma^0_1$-definable equivalence relation $E\neq \mathrm{Id}_1$ on $\omega$ admits a diagonal function."

(iii) Determine the Weihrauch degree of the multi-valued problem that takes as input (an index of) a $\Sigma^0_1$-definable equivalence relation $E\neq \mathrm{Id}_1$ on $\omega$ and outputs a diagonal function for $E$.
artifact.status_search_result: The problem appears as a stated open problem in a 2025 collection of open problems in computability theory and descriptive set theory. No targeted resolution of the class Diag, the reverse-mathematical strength, or the Weihrauch degree of the diagonal-function problem for ceers was found in the literature search.
